Root cause (must be connected to behavior, and it is):
The GSM8K scorer in `src/framework/verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py` restricts strict `#### <number>` extraction to the last 300 characters of the decoded response, and returns 0 if that window has no match (format_score is 0.0 even if a match is the wrong number). This is not in the framework docs and is a false "300 tokens" approximation (300 characters, not tokens). Official GSM8K reasoning is often longer than 300 characters (~45% of the 64-row held-out answers exceed 300 chars; `####` sits at the very end of the reference solution). Early in training, responses are short (mean ~233 tokens at step 1), so the marker can fall inside the window and train reward is nonzero (means ~0.23 then ~0.34, multiples of 1/16). As responses lengthen, the marker is increasingly outside the last 300 characters, or the 1024-token cap cuts the response before `####` is emitted. Reward then collapses to identically 0 (last positive train score step 96 = 0.125; always 0 after). GRPO with all-equal group rewards yields zero advantages, so pg_loss and pg_clipfrac go to 0 and the actor update is only `kl_loss_coef * kl_loss` (coef 0.001). The policy is no longer trained toward correctness and length saturates: response_length mean/min/max = 1024 and clip_ratio = 1.0 by step 150. Held-out greedy eval uses the same scorer: step 100 and step 150 `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 = 0.0` and reward mean@1 = 0.0. Train reward collapse is therefore confirmed on held-out data, not just the train metric.

Symptoms, not causes: zero pg_loss / advantages / returns after the reward dies; response_length clip_ratio → 1; falling late entropy; actor/loss ≈ 0.0002; W&B missing steps 149–150; post-run vLLM EngineDeadError and wandb atexit; CPU_STAGED_DDP / NCCL warmup; val_batch_size deprecation; finite grad-norm spikes.

1. Scorer bug: last-300-character window + strict `####` + format_score 0.
2. Early short responses can still score (evidence the pipeline is not globally broken).
3. Length growth moves `####` out of the window and/or hits max_response_length 1024 before the answer, so score → 0 even when clip_ratio is still 0 (steps ~57, 67) and then for every sample once clip_ratio → 1.
4. GRPO advantage vanishes when every sample in the group scores 0 → pg_loss 0.
5. Only KL term remains; policy locked into long truncated generations.
6. Same scorer on held-out greedy generations at steps 100 and 150 → acc 0.0.

arguments.new_string:
**Verdict: unhealthy.**

The run completed all 150 steps, but the policy stopped receiving a correctness signal and the held-out GSM8K score is 0. The root cause is the GSM8K scorer in `src/framework/verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py`. `extract_solution` keeps only the last `_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300` characters before the strict `#### <number>` match, and the comment treats that as “a safe approximation for 300 tokens.” `compute_score` returns 0 when that window has no match, and `format_score` defaults to 0.0 even when a number is present but wrong. `default_compute_score` dispatches `openai/gsm8k` to this function. The framework reward docs describe a full-string `####` match (1 / 0.1 / 0) and do not mention a 300-character window. Provenance calls the scorer unmodified; the file on the import path (`PYTHONPATH` includes `src/framework`) is not that documented scorer.

This window is not a harmless speed cut. On the 64-row held-out set, official answers are 122–727 characters (median 282.5, mean 316, 45.3% longer than 300 characters; a 500-row train sample is 39.2% longer than 300). The `####` marker itself sits 6–11 characters before the end of every held-out reference, so a short response that ends with `#### N` still scores. Qwen tokenization of those answers is about 2.4 characters per token, so 300 characters is roughly 110–125 tokens, not 300. `prepare_gsm8k.py` only self-checks short `"#### "+ground_truth` strings, which stay inside the window.

Observed training matches that failure mode. With `train_batch_size=4` and `rollout.n=4`, scores are multiples of 1/16. Steps 1–20 have mean `critic/score/mean` 0.228 (mean response length 207, max usually far below 1024). Steps 21–56 rise to 0.339 at mean length 245, so the pipeline can return 1.0 when the marker is in the tail. The first all-zero batch is step 57 (mean length 455, max 799, `response_length/clip_ratio` 0), and step 67 is also all zero with max length 880 and clip ratio 0. Hard truncation is therefore not required to zero the reward: a finished response whose `####` is outside the last 300 characters scores 0. From step 85 the score is almost always 0; the last positive score is step 96 (0.125). Steps 97–148 are identically 0. Response length then saturates at `max_response_length=1024`: clip ratio (fraction of responses with length equal to 1024, `metric_utils.py`) reaches 1.0 at step 106 and is 1.0 for every logged step from 127 through 148. Console step 150 is the same: response length mean/min/max 1024, clip ratio 1.0, score/reward/advantage/return 0, `actor/pg_loss` 0, `actor/pg_clipfrac` 0.

GRPO (`adv_estimator: grpo`, `norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: true`) makes an all-zero group an all-zero advantage. Policy gradient and PPO clip fraction therefore go to 0 on exactly the zero-score steps (61 of them), while `actor/kl_loss` stays nonzero. With `use_kl_loss: true` and `kl_loss_coef: 0.001`, the late actor loss is only the KL term (about 0.0002). The policy is no longer updated toward correct answers and stays locked on 1024-token generations. Rollout–actor Pearson correlation stays 0.973–0.998 and rollout KL stays about 0.006–0.017, so this is not an actor/rollout mismatch. Grad norms stay finite (about 54–1113). Entropy rises early (peak 0.412 at step 79) and falls once length saturates (about 0.13 late).

Held-out eval uses the same scorer. `val_before_train` is false and `test_freq` is 100, so the only evals are steps 100 and 150, greedy (`val_kwargs.do_sample: false`, n=1). Both report `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 = 0.0` and `val-aux/openai/gsm8k/reward/mean@1 = 0.0`. `num_turns` mean/min/max is 2, which is the single-turn agent loop, not a multi-turn failure. Training reward collapse is therefore confirmed on the fixed 64-row held-out set.

**Symptoms, not causes.** Zero advantages, returns, `pg_loss`, and `pg_clipfrac` after the reward dies; `response_length/clip_ratio` → 1; late entropy drop; actor loss collapsing to `0.001 * kl_loss`.

**Not causes.** Offline W&B stops at step 148 (`logging-limitation.txt`); the console has steps 149–150 and “Training Progress: 100%| 150/150” before the post-run vLLM `EngineDeadError` and wandb atexit error. Those are teardown and a logging gap, not a mid-run crash. CPU-staged DDP and expert NCCL warmup in `runtime_lowmem.py` ran and did not desynchronize rollout and actor. `moe_aux_loss_coeff: 0` and `moe_router_load_balancing_type: none`, LR 1e-6, batch 4, and `entropy_coeff: 0` are unusual but do not force exact zero reward on both train batches and greedy held-out eval. Rollout dumps were not retained in this snapshot; the metric timeline, scorer, and answer-length distribution are sufficient.

Zero policy gradient, length saturation, the missing W&B steps 149–150, and the post-run engine teardown are symptoms or logging limits, not the cause.
